old: The 2025 Bear Gulch Fire (~20,000+ acres) burned into the Staircase/Lake Cushman and North Fork Skokomish area; several trails there (Mt. Rose, Mildred Lakes, Dry Creek, Copper Creek) remain closed through Oct 1, 2026, though FS-24 and the Staircase developed area reopened July 8, 2026. text: The 2025 Bear Gulch Fire (~20,000+ acres) burned into the Staircase/Lake Cushman and North Fork Skokomish area. FS-24 and the Forest Service sites around Lake Cushman reopened July 8, 2026; only FS-2451 and the Copper Creek Trail stay closed under the burn-area order, with no end date. This is a different drainage from the South Fork Skokomish/Six Ridge approach used for Olson and doesn’t directly affect it, but verify current trail and road status before a trip.

old: From US-101 at Lake Quinault take North Shore Road about 14 miles to the North/South Shore intersection, then North Fork Quinault Road about 4 miles to the trailhead and ranger station. North Shore is the only way in: South Shore Road is closed by a washout at about mile 8 from US-101, with no reopening date on Olympic National Park's alerts page updated August 27, 2026. The Elwha approach via Whiskey Bend is a genuine alternative but is foot and bike only: Olympic Hot Springs Road has been shut to vehicles beyond Madison Falls since November 2017 flood damage, adding roughly 7 miles each way.
text: From US-101 at Lake Quinault take North Shore Road about 14 miles to the North/South Shore intersection, then North Fork Quinault Road about 4 miles to the trailhead and ranger station. South Shore Road, washed out since 2024, reopened Oct 8, 2026 and leads to Graves Creek; the temporary bridge joining the two shore roads is removed for the winter. The Elwha approach via Whiskey Bend is a genuine alternative but is foot and bike only: Olympic Hot Springs Road has been shut to vehicles beyond Madison Falls since November 2017 flood damage, adding roughly 7 miles each way.

old: Whiskey Bend Road has been closed to vehicles since November 2017 flood damage washed out Olympic Hot Springs Road beyond Madison Falls; Graves Creek Road (Quinault side) reopened May 2026 via a North Shore Road detour after a separate South Shore Road washout. Check the NPS Current Road Conditions page before any trip.

old: SR-20 is paved and generally in good condition but closes seasonally over Washington Pass/Rainy Pass (typically mid-November through April/May depending on snowpack). Silver-Skagit Road is a rough ~39-mile gravel road from Hope, BC, but provides no legal access to Castle Peak: the Hozomeen border gate has been closed to crossing since 2020, with no end date given on the park's fire-closure page updated 14 September 2026, and the road itself has been closed at km 6 for wildfire since 24 July 2026.

old: The NPS gate at the international border at Hozomeen has been closed to vehicle and foot traffic since 2020, until further notice. The Border 2 Fire closed the entire Hozomeen area, including both campground loops, the docks, the Obelisk Trail and the Hozomeen Cross-country Zone, and closed Silver-Skagit Road at the km 6 gate on the B.C. side. Check the park's fire-closure page and B.C. road advisories before planning.
text: The Hozomeen crossing at the international boundary has been closed to vehicles and foot traffic since 2020; enter the U.S. only at a staffed port of entry. On the U.S. side the park has closed the entire Hozomeen area and the Hozomeen Cross-country Zone for the Border 2 Fire, with no end date given in its October 6, 2026 update. Silver-Skagit Road in B.C. reopened October 26, 2026 after its summer wildfire closure, but Skagit Valley Provincial Park stays closed and a fire is still active near km 51. Check both before planning.

old: The NPS gate at the international boundary at Hozomeen has been closed to both vehicle and foot traffic since 2020, and the park's fire-closure page, updated 14 September 2026, still lists it closed with no end date given — crossing there is prohibited and you must use a staffed port of entry. The Silver-Skagit Road has been closed to the public at the km 6 gate since 24 July 2026, when BC Parks closed Skagit Valley Provincial Park for wildfire; the B.C. Ministry of Transportation and Transit advisory, last updated 8 September 2026, gives no end date and keeps the road closed while the park is. On the US side, the park has also closed the entire Hozomeen area and the Hozomeen Cross-country Zone for the Border 2 Fire, with no end date given on the same 14 September 2026 page. Verify all three before committing to a trip.

old: Brush Creek Trail (the final approach corridor toward Whatcom Pass/Indian Mountain) reopened Sept. 2025 after a 3-year closure from the 2022 Brush Creek Fire; Graybeal, Graybeal Stock, and Whatcom Camps remain closed until further notice, with no end date given, as listed on the North Cascades National Park fire-closures page updated September 14, 2026, and the trail is not fully stock-accessible. The Chilliwack River Trail has been cleared of down trees as far as Bear Creek Camp, as listed on the park's trail report of September 3, 2026, but is still brushy north of the Copper Ridge junction. Bear Creek Camp is closed from 2021 fire damage, as still listed on the park's trail-conditions page updated September 17, 2026. A bypass has been built around a prior washout at the end of FR 32 to keep the Hannegan Trailhead reachable — check Mt. Baker Ranger District alerts before driving.

old: Decent gravel for roughly the first 11 miles from WA-207, then narrow, rough, and high-clearance-recommended for the final ~12 miles to Trinity Trailhead; sections beyond Goose Creek have been closed in some years by flood damage and wildfire activity. Storm damage has closed the road to vehicles beyond the Atkinson Flat Campground junction, with no reopening estimate, cutting off the Trinity and Phelps Creek trailheads, and a wildfire closure has also covered the Chiwawa River Road and Phelps Creek Road. Check with the Wenatchee River Ranger District, (509) 548-2550, before you go.
